name: cartography-plugins
description: Workspace-agnostic Claude Code tooling: cartography of a repository by functionality, git commit and pull request conventions executed by narrow agents, a two-pass challenge-then-interview workflow turning a raw idea into a functional specification, and a mirror of the Claude Code agents onto Codex.

plugins.name: cartography
plugins.description: Maps a repository by functionality rather than by code: an index of what lives where, one detail entry per usecase, and the refusal surface. Ships the cartographer and scout agents, the format specification with its templates, and a validator.

plugins.name: git-conventions
plugins.description: Commit and pull request conventions executed by two narrow agents: committer writes a Conventional Commits + Gitmoji message for the staged changes and commits it after a shape check; pr-opener writes a pull request from the commits and opens or updates it. Neither ever stages, pushes, merges or rewrites history.

plugins.name: feature-spec
plugins.description: Turns a raw product idea into a functional specification in two passes: spec-writer runs the mandatory challenge, then interview, then write sequence; spec-second-pass reads the result with another model and amends it with what the first pass left out. Ships the workflow-feature-spec skill with the specification template, which a project may replace with its own. Never invents a missing fact, never settles an open reflection, never publishes anywhere.

plugins.name: codex-mirror
plugins.description: Mirrors a project's Claude Code agents and skills onto Codex: every agent of .claude/agents/ and of each enabled plugin becomes a .codex/agents/*.toml, .claude/skills/ is copied to .agents/skills/, and a model table maps each Claude model to a Codex model. A SessionStart hook reports a stale mirror. Codex cannot load a subagent from a plugin; this is how a plugin's agents reach it.
